subject: Wire instructions: beneficiary flags and who bears intermediary fees

From: Sofia Martinez <sofiam@acme.com>

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Wire instruction question — beneficiary flag and intermediary bank fees

Hi Ben,

We're preparing the May payment for Redwood (invoice 3892) and our bank asked for clarification on two points before they release the wire:

1) Beneficiary flagging: our payments team can set the beneficiary name as the operating entity or the payout entity. For your multi-entity setup, which should appear on the wire to ensure correct matching on your side?

2) Intermediary bank (correspondent) fees: JP Morgan says the wire may incur an intermediary fee in transit. We need to confirm whether Acme should set SHA (split fees), OUR (we pay all), or BEN (you deduct). The invoice was issued to Acme US Holdings; we want to avoid a short payment and incorrect VAT tagging.

I've attached the wire template and the invoice. Can you confirm the exact strings for beneficiary and what fee instruction Redwood prefers?

Thanks,
Sofia

Hi Sofia — thanks for the template and quick heads-up. Short answers first, details after:

- Beneficiary name: Please set the beneficiary to "Redwood Inference, Inc. (US Ops)" and include our internal reference in the beneficiary address line: "Ref: INV-3892 / ACME-8742". That ensures auto-matching into our AR flows.
- Fee instruction: Please instruct OUR only if Acme agrees to cover correspondent fees. Otherwise set SHA and our team will expect a possible short payment equal to the intermediary fee. If you cannot take OUR, set SHA and add an extra line in the payment advice documenting the expected intermediary fee (estimated amount).

A couple of important notes:
- For VAT tagging: when a short payment happens due to intermediary fees, our system will allocate the shortfall as a bank charge and not as VAT — but it creates reconciliation overhead.
- If you want zero reconciliation risk, set OUR. For large recurring payments we can add a remit buffer line to your invoice so you can do SHA without recurring short pays.

Laura/Marissa — can you confirm any accounting constraints on our side for accepting SHA vs OUR for this customer?

Ben

Ben / Marissa — quick accounting note from AP perspective:

- We prefer OUR for single large one-off settlements to avoid revenue recognition friction, but for routine monthly invoices we accept SHA with a reconciliation process.
- If Acme sends SHA, please ask them to include the full trace code and add a separate line in the payment remittance specifying the intermediary charge amount or an "estimated intermediary fee". That line should be labeled clearly (e.g., "Intermediary fee estimated: USD 25.00").
- On our side we will not reclass VAT because of intermediary bank fees; instead we book the fee as a bank expense and we still reconcile the net payment to the invoice. So from a VAT reclaim perspective, the invoice amount remains the taxable base.

Marissa — can ops confirm if including the internal reference in the beneficiary address is sufficient for auto-match? If not, we'll need a payment reference in the swift message itself.

Laura Bennett
Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
